class DiskSpaceTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """A new install, or a part being added, says what it will download and keep, and
    stops before the first download when the filesystem cannot hold it."""

    INSTALLER = (ROOT / "install.sh").read_text()
    STUBS = ('say() { echo "== $*"; }; warn() { echo "WARN $*"; }; '
             'die() { echo "DIE $*"; exit 1; }\n')

    def run_block(self, source, start, end, prelude, free_kb, **env):
        tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()).resolve()
        self.addCleanup(subprocess.run, ["rm", "-rf", str(tmp)])
        (tmp / "bin").mkdir()
        (tmp / "bin/df").write_text(f"#!/bin/sh\necho 'Filesystem 1024-blocks Used Available Capacity Mounted'\n"
                                     f"echo 'disk 999999999 1 {free_kb} 1% /'\n")
        (tmp / "bin/df").chmod(0o755)
        snippet = source[source.index(start):source.index(end)]
        script = f'set -u\nT="$1"; cd "$T"\n{self.STUBS}{prelude}\n{snippet}\necho "NOTED=${{ELM_PI_DISK_NOTED:-}}"'
        clean = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith("ELM_PI_")}
        return subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", script, "t", str(tmp)], capture_output=True, text=True,
                              env={**clean, "PATH": f"{tmp}/bin:/usr/bin:/bin", **env}), tmp

    def installer(self, args="", free_kb=50_000_000, existing=False, **env):
        prelude = f'PREFIX="$T/elm-pi"; PASS_ARGS=({args})'
        if existing:
            prelude += '; mkdir -p "$PREFIX" && touch "$PREFIX/bootstrap.sh"'
        return self.run_block(self.INSTALLER, "# A new install: say what it will download",
                              "# --- 2. get the source", prelude, free_kb, **env)[0]

    def test_a_new_install_says_what_it_takes_and_tells_bootstrap_it_did(self):
        r = self.installer("--with-all")
        self.assertEqual(0, r.returncode, r.stdout + r.stderr)
        self.assertIn("This is a new install. It downloads and keeps about 2.4 GB", r.stdout)
        self.assertIn("the agent's Python", r.stdout)
        self.assertIn("about 1.0 GB more while it runs", r.stdout)
        self.assertIn("NOTED=1", r.stdout)
        plain = self.installer()
        self.assertIn("about 1.0 GB in", plain.stdout)
        self.assertNotIn("Python", plain.stdout)

    def test_too_little_room_stops_before_any_download(self):
        r = self.installer("--with-all", free_kb=2_000_000)          # 2 GB free, 3.4 GB needed
        self.assertEqual(1, r.returncode)
        self.assertIn("DIE only 2.0 GB free", r.stdout)
        self.assertIn("needs about 3.4 GB", r.stdout)
        r = self.installer("--with-all", free_kb=2_000_000, ELM_PI_IGNORE_DISK_SPACE="1")
        self.assertEqual(0, r.returncode)
        self.assertIn("going ahead", r.stdout)

    def test_an_existing_install_is_not_told_again(self):
        r = self.installer("--with-all", existing=True)
        self.assertNotIn("new install", r.stdout)

    def bootstrap(self, free_kb=50_000_000, setup="", python=0, index=0, **env):
        source = (ROOT / "bootstrap.sh").read_text()
        prelude = f'HERE="$T"; WITH_PYTHON={python}; WITH_PYPI_INDEX={index}; {setup}'
        return self.run_block(source, "# --- disk space", "# --- 1. Node", prelude, free_kb, **env)[0]

    def test_bootstrap_counts_only_what_this_run_adds(self):
        new = self.bootstrap()
        self.assertIn("downloads and keeps about 1.0 GB", new.stdout)
        gaining = self.bootstrap(setup="mkdir -p node_modules", python=1, index=1)
        self.assertIn("about 1.4 GB", gaining.stdout)                 # Python + index kept, no base
        self.assertNotIn("Node, pi", gaining.stdout)
        nothing = self.bootstrap(setup="mkdir -p node_modules agent/python/env/bin && touch agent/python/env/bin/python && chmod 755 agent/python/env/bin/python", python=1)
        self.assertNotIn("disk space", nothing.stdout)
        quiet = self.bootstrap(ELM_PI_DISK_NOTED="1")                  # install.sh said it already
        self.assertNotIn("disk space", quiet.stdout)
        full = self.bootstrap(free_kb=500_000, ELM_PI_DISK_NOTED="1")  # ...but the check still runs
        self.assertEqual(1, full.returncode)

    def test_both_scripts_use_the_same_figures(self):
        bootstrap = (ROOT / "bootstrap.sh").read_text()
        self.assertIn("DISK_BASE_MB=1000; DISK_PYTHON_MB=1000; DISK_PYPI_KEPT_MB=400; DISK_PYPI_TEMP_MB=1000", bootstrap)
        for figure in ("DISK_KEEP=1000;", "DISK_KEEP + 1000", "DISK_KEEP + 400", "DISK_TEMP=1000"):
            self.assertIn(figure, self.INSTALLER)

"""Real tools' colour, end to end: printed straight to pi, read plain by the model, drawn in colour.

templates/shell/colour.sh makes git, ls, grep, rg, fd, jq, diff, ruff,
shellcheck and pytest colour what they print when stdout is the pipe pi reads;
templates/extensions/command-output.ts then hands the model plain text and the
display the colour. Each case here runs a real command on a real fixture (git
repositories with history, renames, binaries and a conflict; a directory of
links, executables and dotfiles; text to search; JSON; Python and shell with
lint findings; pytest suites that pass and fail) twice in one bash process:
once as pi's bash tool runs it - `<shellCommandPrefix>\\n<command>`, stdout a
pipe - and once with NO_COLOR=1, which turns every wrapper off.

Each output is then turned into the result pi's bash tool would return (its own
OutputAccumulator, so long outputs are truncated and saved as pi saves them),
passed through the extension's tool_result handler and drawn by its renderer,
all in one node process. One test method per case and invariant proves:

- the model's copy has no escape codes or `\\r` and is exactly what the
  NO_COLOR run gave the model: taking colour out never changes text;
- the colour reaches the display (details.colour, and the note to the model)
  exactly when the tool coloured, and its text is the model's text;
- every drawn panel row keeps the panel's structure (terminal background,
  margin, the box tint, the full width), and shows the plain run's lines;
- wrapped into a narrow panel, no character is lost or invented;
- a long output's collapsed view is its plain head and tail;
- a truncated output's saved file becomes exactly what the plain run printed,
  the model's tail ends that output, and the view names the file.

Known bugs these cases found are expected failures, each naming the bug.

The tests skip when node, the pi packages or a tool are missing; pytest cases
skip when pytest is not installed.
"""

            f") 2>{shlex.quote(str(logs / (str(i) + '.err')))}\nprintf '\\n@@{i}>%d\\n' $?\n")
    proc = subprocess.run([bash, "-c", "".join(parts)], cwd=D["dir"], capture_output=True,
                          text=True, env=environ(), timeout=300)
    results = {}
    for i, c in enumerate(cases):
        m = re.search(rf"\n@@{i}<\n(.*?)\n@@{i}>(\d+)\n", proc.stdout, re.S)
        if m is None:
            results[c.slug] = None
            continue
        log = logs / str(i)
        err = (logs / f"{i}.err").read_text()
        calls = parse_log(log.read_text()) if log.exists() else []
        results[c.slug] = (m.group(1), err, int(m.group(2)), calls)
    shutil.rmtree(logs, ignore_errors=True)
    return results


class WrapperCases(unittest.TestCase):
    CASES = []
    BASH = "bash"

    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.results = run_batch(cls.CASES, cls.BASH)

    def check(self, c):
        if c.skip and c.skip():
            raise unittest.SkipTest(c.skip())
        result = self.results[c.slug]
        self.assertIsNotNone(result, f"case {c.slug} did not finish")
        out, err, status, calls = result
        if c.calls is not None:
            self.assertEqual([(n, a) for n, a, _ in calls], [(n, list(a)) for n, a in c.calls])
        if c.envs is not None:
            self.assertTrue(calls, "the tool was not called")
            got = calls[-1][2]
            self.assertEqual({k: got[k] for k in c.envs}, c.envs)
        if c.out is not None:
            self.assertEqual(out, c.out)
        if c.has is not None:
            self.assertIn(c.has, out)
        if c.lacks is not None:
            self.assertNotIn(c.lacks, out)
        if c.err is not None:
            self.assertEqual(err, c.err)
        self.assertEqual(status, c.status)


def generate(cls):
    for c in cls.CASES:
        name = "test_" + re.sub(r"\W+", "_", c.slug).strip("_")
        assert not hasattr(cls, name), f"duplicate case {name}"

        def test(self, c=c):
            self.check(c)
        if c.xfail:
            test = unittest.expectedFailure(test)
        test.__doc__ = c.xfail or c.cmd.splitlines()[-1][:100]
        setattr(cls, name, test)
    return cls

PACKAGE_LIBRARIES = {"@xl0/pi-lovely-notebook": ["@xl0/lovely-notebook"]}


@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def package_source(name):
    """Every source file of an installed package (or pi's dist), concatenated."""
    base = PI_DIST if name == "pi" else NPM / name
    if not base.is_dir():
        return None
    parts = [package_source(lib) or "" for lib in PACKAGE_LIBRARIES.get(name, [])]
    for path in sorted(base.rglob("*")):
        if path.suffix in {".ts", ".js", ".mjs", ".cjs"} and path.is_file() \
                and "node_modules" not in path.relative_to(base).parts and not path.name.endswith(".map"):
            parts.append(path.read_text(errors="replace"))
    return "\n".join(parts)

CAPTURES = {"{N}": r"(\d[\d,]*|[a-z]+)", "{L}": r"(\d+(?:, \d+)+)", "{V}": r"(v?\d+(?:\.\d+)+)"}


def parse_number(text):
    if text in NUMBER_WORDS or text.capitalize() in map(str.capitalize, NUMBER_WORDS):
        return NUMBER_WORDS[text.lower()]
    if re.fullmatch(r"\d[\d,]*", text):
        return int(text.replace(",", ""))
    if re.fullmatch(r"\d+(?:, \d+)+", text):
        return [int(x) for x in text.split(", ")]
    return text


def _number(self, doc, claim, actual):
    text = FLAT.get(doc) or PROMPT_FLAT.get(doc)
    pattern = re.escape(claim)
    for token, capture in CAPTURES.items():
        pattern = pattern.replace(re.escape(token), capture)
    match = re.search(pattern, text, re.I)
    self.assertIsNotNone(match, f"{doc} no longer says {claim!r}")
    said = parse_number(match.group(1).lower() if match.group(1).isalpha() else match.group(1))
    if isinstance(actual, tuple):           # measured from an installed package
        package, source_pattern = actual
        source = package_source(package)
        if source is None:
            self.skipTest(f"{package} is not installed in this checkout")
        actual = int(re.search(source_pattern, source).group(1))
    if isinstance(actual, set):
        self.assertIn(said, actual, f"{doc}: {match.group(0)!r}")
    else:
        self.assertEqual(actual, said, f"{doc}: {match.group(0)!r}")

class RequestLineEdgeTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_client_that_sends_nothing_gets_nothing_and_no_log(self):
        proxy = proxy_for(SHIPPED)
        self.assertEqual(b"", exchange(proxy, b""))
        self.assertEqual([], log_lines(proxy))

    def test_tls_hello_without_connect_is_refused(self):
        # a client that forgot it is talking to a proxy
        hello = b"\x16\x03\x01\x00\xa5\x01\x00\x00\xa1\x03\x03" + bytes(range(32, 96)) + b"\r\n\r\n"
        proxy = proxy_for(SHIPPED)
        self.assertTrue(exchange(proxy, hello).startswith(b"HTTP/1.1 403 "))
        self.assertTrue(log_lines(proxy)[0].startswith("REJECTED "))

    def test_head_sent_one_byte_at_a_time(self):
        proxy = proxy_for(SHIPPED)
        client, thread = start_handle(proxy)
        for b in b"CONNECT evil.com:443 HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n":
            client.send(bytes([b]))
        reply = recv_all(client)
        client.close()
        thread.join(5)
        self.assertTrue(reply.startswith(b"HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden\r\n"))
        self.assertEqual(["REJECTED evil.com:443 not on the allowlist"], log_lines(proxy))

    def test_refusal_without_half_close(self):
        # a complete head is enough; the proxy must not wait for EOF to answer
        proxy = proxy_for(SHIPPED)
        reply = exchange(proxy, b"CONNECT evil.com:443 HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n", shut=False)
        self.assertTrue(reply.startswith(b"HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden\r\n"))

    def test_bytes_pipelined_after_a_refused_connect_are_not_sent_anywhere(self):
        proxy = proxy_for(SHIPPED)
        reply = exchange(proxy, b"CONNECT evil.com:443 HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n\x16\x03\x01secret")
        self.assertNotIn(b"secret", reply)
        self.assertNotIn("secret", Path(proxy.log_path).read_text())

    def test_latin1_method_survives_into_the_reason(self):
        proxy = proxy_for(SHIPPED)
        _, headers, _ = split_response(exchange(proxy, "G\xc9T /x HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n".encode("latin-1")))
        self.assertEqual("plain HTTP G\xc9T without a host", headers["x-elm-pi-reason"])

class TunnelTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """CONNECT to an allowed host: a local echo server on 127.0.0.1, listed."""

    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.echo = Echo()
        cls.target = b"127.0.0.1:%d" % cls.echo.port

    @classmethod
    def tearDownClass(cls):
        cls.echo.close()

    def open_tunnel(self, proxy=None, extra=b""):
        proxy = proxy or proxy_for(["127.0.0.1"])
        client, thread = start_handle(proxy)
        client.sendall(b"CONNECT " + self.target + b" HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n" + extra)
        return proxy, client, thread

    ESTABLISHED = b"HTTP/1.1 200 Connection Established\r\n\r\n"

    def test_answers_connection_established(self):
        _, client, thread = self.open_tunnel()
        self.assertEqual(self.ESTABLISHED, recv_exactly(client, len(self.ESTABLISHED)))
        client.close()
        thread.join(5)

    def test_bytes_flow_both_ways(self):
        _, client, thread = self.open_tunnel()
        recv_exactly(client, len(self.ESTABLISHED))
        client.sendall(b"ping")
        self.assertEqual(b"ping", recv_exactly(client, 4))
        client.close()
        thread.join(5)

    def test_bytes_pipelined_behind_connect_reach_the_destination(self):
        # the ClientHello-in-the-same-packet case the docstring describes
        _, client, thread = self.open_tunnel(extra=b"\x16\x03\x01early")
        got = recv_exactly(client, len(self.ESTABLISHED) + 8)
        self.assertEqual(self.ESTABLISHED + b"\x16\x03\x01early", got)
        client.close()
        thread.join(5)

    def test_every_byte_value_passes_unchanged(self):
        _, client, thread = self.open_tunnel()
        recv_exactly(client, len(self.ESTABLISHED))
        payload = bytes(range(256)) * 4
        client.sendall(payload)
        self.assertEqual(payload, recv_exactly(client, len(payload)))
        client.close()
        thread.join(5)

    def test_a_megabyte_round_trips(self):
        _, client, thread = self.open_tunnel()
        recv_exactly(client, len(self.ESTABLISHED))
        payload = os.urandom(1 << 20)
        sender = threading.Thread(target=client.sendall, args=(payload,))
        sender.start()
        got = recv_exactly(client, len(payload), timeout=20)
        sender.join(20)
        self.assertEqual(payload, got)
        client.close()
        thread.join(5)

    def test_closing_the_client_ends_the_tunnel(self):
        _, client, thread = self.open_tunnel()
        recv_exactly(client, len(self.ESTABLISHED))
        client.close()
        thread.join(5)
        self.assertFalse(thread.is_alive())

    def test_an_allowed_tunnel_is_not_logged(self):
        proxy, client, thread = self.open_tunnel()
        recv_exactly(client, len(self.ESTABLISHED))
        client.close()
        thread.join(5)
        self.assertEqual([], log_lines(proxy))

    def test_destination_that_speaks_first(self):
        greeter = Echo(greeting=b"220 hello\r\n")
        self.addCleanup(greeter.close)
        client, thread = start_handle(proxy_for(["127.0.0.1"]))
        client.sendall(b"CONNECT 127.0.0.1:%d HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n" % greeter.port)
        self.assertEqual(self.ESTABLISHED + b"220 hello\r\n",
                         recv_exactly(client, len(self.ESTABLISHED) + 11))
        client.close()
        thread.join(5)

    def test_unreachable_destination_is_logged_as_failed(self):
        port = free_port()
        proxy = proxy_for(["127.0.0.1"])
        reply = exchange(proxy, b"CONNECT 127.0.0.1:%d HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n" % port)
        self.assertEqual(b"", reply)       # no 200, and no 403 that blames the policy
        [line] = log_lines(proxy)
        self.assertTrue(line.startswith("FAILED   127.0.0.1:%d " % port), line)
        self.assertIn("refused", line.lower())

    def test_non_numeric_port_on_an_allowed_host_fails_without_dialling(self):
        proxy = proxy_for(["127.0.0.1"])
        self.assertEqual(b"", exchange(proxy, b"CONNECT 127.0.0.1:https HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n"))
        [line] = log_lines(proxy)
        self.assertTrue(line.startswith("FAILED   127.0.0.1:https unexpected ValueError("), line)


class OpenModeTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """--allow '*': nothing is gated, every new destination is recorded once."""

    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):

    @classmethod

        client, thread = start_handle(proxy)
        client.sendall(b"CONNECT %s:%d HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n" % (host.encode(), self.echo.port))

        client.close()

class PlainForwardTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Plain HTTP to an allowed host: rewritten to origin-form, headers kept."""

    def setUp(self):
        self.origin = Origin()
        self.addCleanup(self.origin.close)
        self.proxy = proxy_for(["127.0.0.1"])
        self.base = b"http://127.0.0.1:%d" % self.origin.port

    def send(self, request):
        reply = exchange(self.proxy, request, shut=False)
        return reply, self.origin.wait()

    def test_request_line_becomes_origin_form(self):
        _, seen = self.send(b"GET " + self.base + b"/a/b?c=1 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\n\r\n")
        self.assertEqual(b"GET /a/b?c=1 HTTP/1.1", seen.split(b"\r\n")[0])

    def test_headers_pass_verbatim(self):
        _, seen = self.send(b"GET " + self.base + b"/ HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\nX-Odd:  keep  me \r\n\r\n")
        self.assertEqual(b"Host: x\r\nX-Odd:  keep  me \r\n\r\n", seen.split(b"\r\n", 1)[1])

    def test_missing_path_becomes_slash(self):
        _, seen = self.send(b"GET " + self.base + b" HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n")
        self.assertEqual(b"GET / HTTP/1.1", seen.split(b"\r\n")[0])

    def test_http_version_is_kept(self):
        _, seen = self.send(b"GET " + self.base + b"/v HTTP/1.0\r\n\r\n")
        self.assertEqual(b"GET /v HTTP/1.0", seen.split(b"\r\n")[0])

    def test_method_is_uppercased(self):
        _, seen = self.send(b"delete " + self.base + b"/d HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n")
        self.assertEqual(b"DELETE /d HTTP/1.1", seen.split(b"\r\n")[0])

    def test_pipelined_body_is_forwarded(self):
        _, seen = self.send(b"POST " + self.base + b"/p HTTP/1.1\r\nContent-Length: 5\r\n\r\nhello")
        self.assertTrue(seen.endswith(b"\r\n\r\nhello"), seen)

    def test_origin_reply_reaches_the_client_verbatim(self):
        reply, _ = self.send(b"GET " + self.base + b"/ HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n")
        self.assertEqual(Origin.RESPONSE, reply)

    def test_allowed_plain_request_is_not_logged(self):
        self.send(b"GET " + self.base + b"/ HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n")
        self.assertEqual([], log_lines(self.proxy))

    # A client that half-closes after sending its request (nc -N,
    # shutdown(SHUT_WR)) still gets the response: EOF is passed on, not fatal.
    def test_half_closed_client_still_gets_the_response(self):
        reply = exchange(self.proxy, b"GET " + self.base + b"/ HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n", shut=True)
        self.assertEqual(Origin.RESPONSE, reply)

    # The authority ends at "?" as well as "/": "http://host:port?q" is host:port.
    def test_query_without_path_is_forwarded(self):
        _, seen = self.send(b"GET " + self.base + b"?q=1 HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n")
        self.assertEqual(b"GET /?q=1 HTTP/1.1", (seen or b"").split(b"\r\n")[0])


class UpstreamTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """A campus proxy in the environment is chained to. The upstream here is a
    loopback fake, so allowlisted names are never resolved or dialled."""

    def chain(self, upstream):
        self.addCleanup(upstream.close)
        return proxy_for(SHIPPED, ("127.0.0.1", upstream.port))

    def test_connect_head_is_passed_on_verbatim(self):
        up = Upstream()
        head = b"CONNECT pypi.org:443 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: pypi.org:443\r\nUser-Agent: pip\r\n\r\n"
        exchange(self.chain(up), head)
        self.assertEqual(head, up.wait())

    def test_upstream_reply_is_relayed_not_replaced(self):
        reply = b"HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established\r\nVia: 1.1 campus\r\n\r\n"
        up = Upstream(reply=(reply,))
        got = exchange(self.chain(up), b"CONNECT pypi.org:443 HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n")
        self.assertEqual(reply, got)

    def test_tunnel_through_upstream(self):
        up = Upstream()
        client, thread = start_handle(self.chain(up))
        client.sendall(b"CONNECT files.pythonhosted.org:443 HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n")
        recv_exactly(client, len(up.reply[0]))
        client.sendall(b"PING")
        self.assertEqual(b"PING", recv_exactly(client, 4))
        client.close()
        thread.join(5)

    def test_pipelined_bytes_go_to_upstream(self):
        up = Upstream()
        head = b"CONNECT pypi.org:443 HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n"
        client, thread = start_handle(self.chain(up))
        client.sendall(head + b"\x16\x03\x01hello")
        recv_exactly(client, len(up.reply[0]) + 8)
        client.close()
        thread.join(5)
        self.assertEqual(head + b"\x16\x03\x01hello", up.wait())

    def test_refusal_is_relayed_and_tunnel_not_opened(self):
        reply = b"HTTP/1.1 407 Proxy Authentication Required\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\n\r\n"
        up = Upstream(reply=(reply,))
        client, thread = start_handle(self.chain(up))
        client.sendall(b"CONNECT pypi.org:443 HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n")
        self.assertEqual(reply, recv_exactly(client, len(reply)))
        try:
            client.sendall(b"PING")
        except OSError:
            pass
        self.assertEqual(b"", recv_all(client, timeout=3))
        client.close()
        thread.join(5)

    def test_reply_split_across_packets_is_read_whole(self):
        up = Upstream(reply=(b"HTTP/1.1 2", b"00 OK\r\n", b"\r\n"))
        client, thread = start_handle(self.chain(up))
        client.sendall(b"CONNECT pypi.org:443 HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n")
        self.assertEqual(b"HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\n\r\n", recv_exactly(client, 19))
        client.sendall(b"PING")
        self.assertEqual(b"PING", recv_exactly(client, 4))
        client.close()
        thread.join(5)

    def test_upstream_that_hangs_up_gives_the_client_nothing(self):
        up = Upstream(reply=(), hang_up=True)
        self.assertEqual(b"", exchange(self.chain(up), b"CONNECT pypi.org:443 HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n"))

    def test_unlisted_host_is_refused_before_upstream(self):
        up = Upstream()
        proxy = self.chain(up)
        reply = exchange(proxy, b"CONNECT evil.com:443 HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n")
        self.assertTrue(reply.startswith(b"HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden"))
        self.assertEqual(0, up.accepted)

    def test_unlisted_plain_http_is_refused_before_upstream(self):
        up = Upstream()
        reply = exchange(self.chain(up), b"GET http://evil.com/ HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n")
        self.assertTrue(reply.startswith(b"HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden"))
        self.assertEqual(0, up.accepted)

    def test_plain_http_goes_to_upstream_in_absolute_form(self):
        up = Upstream(reply=(b"HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\n\r\n",), hang_up=True)
        head = b"GET http://pypi.org/simple/ HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: pypi.org\r\n\r\n"
        exchange(self.chain(up), head)
        self.assertEqual(head, up.wait())

    def test_unreachable_upstream_is_logged(self):
        proxy = proxy_for(SHIPPED, ("127.0.0.1", free_port()))
        self.assertEqual(b"", exchange(proxy, b"CONNECT pypi.org:443 HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n"))
        [line] = log_lines(proxy)
        self.assertTrue(line.startswith("FAILED   pypi.org:443 "), line)

    # The status code decides, not "200" anywhere in the line.
    def test_status_code_not_reason_phrase_decides(self):
        reply = b"HTTP/1.1 403 Blocked 200 times\r\n\r\n"
        up = Upstream(reply=(reply,))
        client, thread = start_handle(self.chain(up))
        client.sendall(b"CONNECT pypi.org:443 HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n")
        recv_exactly(client, len(reply))
        try:
            client.sendall(b"PING")
        except OSError:
            pass
        leaked = recv_all(client, timeout=2)
        client.close()
        thread.join(5)
        self.assertEqual(b"", leaked)

_BASE = {}


def configure_base():
    """One install rendered from this checkout, copied for each case."""
    if "dir" not in _BASE:
        base = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()).resolve() / "base"
        base.mkdir()
        shutil.copy2(ROOT / "configure.sh", base / "configure.sh")
        for name in ("lib", "config", "scripts", "templates"):
            shutil.copytree(ROOT / name, base / name, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("__pycache__"))
        render = [PY, str(base / "scripts/elm_config.py"), "--root", str(base)]
        subprocess.run([*render, "init"], check=True, capture_output=True)
        for name in ("models.json", "settings.json"):
            subprocess.run([*render, "render", str(base / "templates" / name), str(base / "agent" / name)],
                           check=True, capture_output=True)
        touch(base / ".node/bin/curl", FAKE_CURL, 0o755)
        # Run each once (configure.sh stops at the missing key) so the cases do not wait on the check.
        subprocess.run([str(base / ".node/bin/curl"), "warm"], capture_output=True)
        subprocess.run([str(base / "configure.sh")], capture_output=True, cwd=base,
                       env={"PATH": "/usr/bin:/bin", "HOME": str(base), "ELM_PI_PYTHON": PY})
        (base / "curl.log").unlink(missing_ok=True)
        BASELINE.update({rel: (base / rel).read_text() for rel in STATE_FILES})
        _BASE["dir"] = base
    return _BASE["dir"]


@generate
class ConfigureTests(Batch):
    """configure.sh, run whole: the gateway's answer, the smoke test, and the merge."""

    CASES = CONFIGURE_CASES

    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        try:
            super().setUpClass()
        finally:
            shutil.rmtree(configure_base().parent, ignore_errors=True)
            _BASE.clear()

    @classmethod
    def prepare(cls, case, d):
        kw = case.kw
        shutil.rmtree(d)
        base = configure_base()
        shutil.copytree(base, d, symlinks=True)
        # macOS checks each new executable the first time it runs: these two
        # are links to the base install's copies, which have already run.
        for rel in ("configure.sh", ".node/bin/curl"):
            (d / rel).unlink()
            os.link(base / rel, d / rel)
        touch(d / ".env", kw["env_file"], 0o600)
        touch(d / "gateway.out", kw["gateway"] if isinstance(kw["gateway"], str) else json.dumps(kw["gateway"]))
        touch(d / "chat.out", kw["chat"] if isinstance(kw["chat"], str) else json.dumps(kw["chat"]))
        if kw["models_rc"] is not None:
            touch(d / "models.rc", str(kw["models_rc"]))
        if kw["models"] is not None:
            touch(d / "agent/models.json", json.dumps(kw["models"]))
        if kw["settings"] is not None:
            touch(d / "agent/settings.json", json.dumps(kw["settings"]))

    @classmethod
    def body(cls, case, d):
        env = f"env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME={q(d)} ELM_PI_PYTHON={q(PY)}"
        run = f"{env} ./configure.sh " + " ".join(q(a) for a in case.kw["args"])
        if case.kw["twice"]:
            save = ('"$PY" -c ' + q("import json,sys; print(json.dumps({r: open(r).read() for r in sys.argv[1:]}))")
                    + " agent/model-ids.json agent/models.json agent/settings.json > first.json")
            run = f"{run} >/dev/null 2>&1\n{save}\n{run}"
        return "\n".join([f"cd {q(d)}", f"PY={q(PY)}", run])

class PrefixTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """ELM_PI_PREFIX as typed becomes the absolute folder; its parent is created, or the reason given."""

    def prefix(self, value, cwd, home):
        env = {"PATH": "/usr/bin:/bin", "HOME": str(home)}
        if value is not None:
            env["ELM_PI_PREFIX"] = value
        script = "set -euo pipefail\n" + PREFIX_NORMALISE + 'printf "%s" "$PREFIX"\n'
        return subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", script], cwd=cwd, env=env, capture_output=True,
                              text=True, check=True).stdout

    def test_every_spelling_becomes_the_absolute_folder(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            d = Path(directory).resolve()
            home, here = d / "home", d / "here"
            home.mkdir(); here.mkdir()
            cases = {
                None: f"{home}/.local/share/elm-pi",
                f"{home}/sandbox/elm-pi": f"{home}/sandbox/elm-pi",
                "~/sandbox/elm-pi": f"{home}/sandbox/elm-pi",           # a quoted ~
                "~": str(home),
                "sandbox/elm-pi": f"{here}/sandbox/elm-pi",             # relative to where it ran
                "./elm-pi": f"{here}/./elm-pi",
                f"{home}/sandbox/elm-pi/": f"{home}/sandbox/elm-pi",
                f"{home}/sandbox/elm-pi//": f"{home}/sandbox/elm-pi",
                "/": "/",
                "~user/x": f"{here}/~user/x",                           # not ours to expand
            }
            for value, expected in cases.items():
                with self.subTest(ELM_PI_PREFIX=value):
                    self.assertEqual(expected, self.prefix(value, here, home))

    def make_parent(self, prefix):
        script = "\n".join(["set -euo pipefail", STUBS, f"PREFIX={q(prefix)}", MAKE_PARENT, "make_parent", "echo made"])
        return subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", script], capture_output=True, text=True)

    def test_missing_folders_above_the_install_are_created(self):

templates/extensions/pi-permission-system/config.json is filled in the way
bootstrap.sh fills it (@INSTALL_DIR@, @AGENT_DIR@) into a temporary install,
then the installed @gotgenes/pi-permission-system package - loaded with jiti,
as pi loads it - decides each case:

- a bash command goes through tree-sitter's parse and resolveBashCommandCheck,
  the function the tool-call gate uses, so chains, substitutions, wrappers
  (env, sudo, bash -c) and last-match-wins precedence are the package's own;
  then through templates/extensions/command-guard.ts, which pi runs beside the
  gate and which denies a spelling of a denied command the gate's rules miss
  (`'ssh' host`, `sudo ssh host`). A call either one blocks is refused, so a
  case's decision is the gate's unless the guard denies what the gate did not;
- a command's path tokens go through the bash path gate (cat .env);
- a file tool's path is resolved on the path and external_directory surfaces,
  and the Pi infrastructure read list is checked with the package's matcher;
- the config itself loads with no issues.

Each case asserts the exact decision (allow / ask / deny) and the rule that
made it, and a deny carries the rule's reason to the model. HOME is a
temporary folder, so ~ in the rules never names the real home. One node
process answers every case in the file. Cases marked BUG are known gaps,
kept as expected failures. The tests skip on a checkout that has not been
bootstrapped.

import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
SANDBOX = ROOT / "lib/sandbox.sh"


def bash(script: str, env=None, check=True) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return subprocess.run(
        ["bash", "-c", f'set -euo pipefail; source "{SANDBOX}"\n{script}'],
        check=check,
        text=True,
        capture_output=True,
        env=env if env is not None else dict(os.environ),
    )


def fake_python(directory: Path, name: str, exit_code: int) -> Path:
    """A stand-in interpreter that answers elm_python_check with exit_code."""
    path = directory / name
    path.write_text(f"#!/bin/sh\nexit {exit_code}\n")
    path.chmod(0o755)
    return path


class ScrubListTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_install_sh_carries_the_same_scrub_lists(self):
        # install.sh runs before lib/sandbox.sh is on disk, so it has a copy.
        pattern = re.compile(r'^(ELM_SCRUB_(?:PREFIXES|NAMES|KEEP))="([^"]*)"', re.M)
        library = dict(pattern.findall(SANDBOX.read_text()))
        installer = dict(pattern.findall((ROOT / "install.sh").read_text()))
        self.assertEqual(3, len(library))
        self.assertEqual(library, installer)

class PythonSelectionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def check(self, path: Path) -> int:
        return bash(f'elm_python_check "{path}"', check=False).returncode

    def test_check_reports_why_an_interpreter_is_refused(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            d = Path(directory)
            self.assertEqual(0, self.check(fake_python(d, "good", 0)))
            self.assertEqual(10, self.check(fake_python(d, "old", 10)))
            self.assertEqual(11, self.check(fake_python(d, "conda", 11)))
            self.assertEqual(1, self.check(d / "missing"))
            shims = d / ".pyenv/shims"
            shims.mkdir(parents=True)
            self.assertEqual(13, self.check(fake_python(shims, "python3", 0)))
        self.assertEqual(1, bash('elm_python_check python3', check=False).returncode)  # not absolute

    def test_check_accepts_the_interpreter_running_these_tests(self):
        # check.sh runs the suite on the interpreter elm_select_python chose.
        import sys
        self.assertIn(self.check(Path(sys.executable)), (0, 11, 12))

    def test_explicit_choice_is_honoured_or_refused_but_never_replaced(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            d = Path(directory)
            for code, ok in ((0, True), (11, True), (12, True), (10, False), (13, False)):
                py = fake_python(d, f"py{code}", code)
                env = {**os.environ, "ELM_PI_PYTHON": str(py)}
                result = bash('elm_select_python "" && echo "$ELM_PI_PYTHON" || echo "ERR $ELM_PY_ERROR"',
                              env=env)
                if ok:
                    self.assertEqual(str(py), result.stdout.strip())
                else:
                    self.assertTrue(result.stdout.startswith("ERR ELM_PI_PYTHON="), result.stdout)

            (d / "agent/python-path").write_text(f"{py}\n")
            env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k != "ELM_PI_PYTHON"}
            for mode in ("", "fast"):
                out = bash(f'elm_select_python "{d}" {mode}; echo "$ELM_PI_PYTHON"', env=env).stdout
                self.assertEqual(str(py), out.strip())

            (d / "conda/bin").mkdir()

            env["PATH"] = f"{d / 'conda/bin'}:{env['PATH']}"

        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:

def guard_capable_node():
    """The bundled node, or else one on PATH new enough for the guard
    (module.registerHooks, Node 22.15+): CI and a fresh clone have no .node."""
    import shutil
    bundled = ROOT / ".node/bin/node"
    if bundled.exists():
        return bundled
    found = shutil.which("node")
    if found and subprocess.run([found, "-e", "process.exit(typeof require('node:module').registerHooks === 'function' ? 0 : 1)"],
                                capture_output=True).returncode == 0:
        return Path(found)
    return None


class NodeGuardTests(unittest.TestCase):

            script = (
                'let out = [process.env.LD_LIBRARY_PATH, "ELM_PI_STASH__LD_LIBRARY_PATH" in process.env];'
                'try { out.push(require("elm-probe")); } catch (e) { out.push(e.message.startsWith("elm-pi: refusing")); }'
                'import("elm-probe").then(() => out.push("loaded"), (e) => out.push(e.message.startsWith("elm-pi: refusing")))'
                '.then(() => console.log(JSON.stringify(out)));'
            )
            env = {**os.environ, "ELM_PI_STASH__LD_LIBRARY_PATH": "/conda/lib"}
            env.pop("ELM_PI_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_MODULES", None)
            out = subprocess.run([str(self.NODE), "--import", str(ROOT / "lib/node-guard.mjs"), "-e", script],
                                 cwd=d, env=env, text=True, capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
            self.assertEqual('["/conda/lib",false,true,true]', out.strip())
            env["ELM_PI_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_MODULES"] = "1"
            out = subprocess.run([str(self.NODE), "--import", str(ROOT / "lib/node-guard.mjs"), "-e", script],
                                 cwd=d, env=env, text=True, capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
            self.assertEqual('["/conda/lib",false,"loaded","loaded"]', out.strip())

        environment = {**os.environ, **env}
        if "ELM_PI_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_MODULES" not in env:
            environment.pop("ELM_PI_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_MODULES", None)
        return subprocess.run([str(self.NODE), "--import", str(guard), "--input-type=module", "-e", script],
                              cwd=cwd, env=environment, text=True, capture_output=True)

            (d / "real/inst/lib/node-guard.mjs").write_text((ROOT / "lib/node-guard.mjs").read_text())
            own = d / "real/inst/agent/npm/node_modules/p/index.js"
            own.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
            own.write_text("1")
            (d / "link").symlink_to(d / "real")
            via_link = d / "link/inst/agent/npm/node_modules/p/index.js"
            script = ('import vm from "node:vm";'
                      'try { vm.runInThisContext("1", { filename: process.argv[1] }); console.log("ran"); }'
                      'catch (e) { console.log(e.message); }')
            out = subprocess.run([str(self.NODE), "--import", str(d / "link/inst/lib/node-guard.mjs"),
                                  "--input-type=module", "-e", script, str(via_link)],
                                 cwd=d, text=True, capture_output=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
            self.assertEqual("ran", out)

    def test_jiti_cannot_take_a_package_from_above_the_install(self):
        # The case the guard exists for: an extension imports a package the
        # install lacks, and jiti's own resolver finds it in a node_modules
        # above the install. Refused under the guard; loaded without it.
        package = next((p for p in (ROOT / "node_modules/jiti", ROOT / "agent/npm/node_modules/jiti")
                        if (p / "lib/jiti.mjs").exists()), None)
        if package is None:
            self.skipTest("jiti is not installed in this checkout")
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            d = Path(os.path.realpath(directory))
            leak = d / "above/node_modules/leakpkg/index.js"
            leak.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
            leak.write_text('module.exports = "leaked";\n')
            install = d / "above/inst"
            (install / "lib").mkdir(parents=True)
            (install / "lib/node-guard.mjs").write_text((ROOT / "lib/node-guard.mjs").read_text())
            (install / "agent").mkdir()
            (install / "agent/ext.ts").write_text('import leak from "leakpkg";\nexport default leak;\n')
            # jiti is the install's own, as pi's is: one from outside would be refused itself.
            shutil.copytree(package, install / "node_modules/jiti")
            jiti = install / "node_modules/jiti/lib/jiti.mjs"
            script = ('const { createJiti } = await import(process.argv[1]);'
                      'const jiti = createJiti(import.meta.url, { fsCache: false, moduleCache: false });'
                      'try { console.log(String((await jiti.import(process.argv[2], { default: true })))); }'
                      'catch (e) { console.log(e.message.startsWith("elm-pi: refusing") ? "refused" : e.message); }')
            args = [str(self.NODE), "--import", str(install / "lib/node-guard.mjs"), "--input-type=module", "-e",
                    script, str(jiti), str(install / "agent/ext.ts")]
            env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k != "ELM_PI_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_MODULES"}
            guarded = subprocess.run(args, cwd=install, env=env, text=True, capture_output=True, check=True)
            self.assertEqual("refused", guarded.stdout.strip(), guarded.stderr)
            open_ = subprocess.run(args, cwd=install, env={**env, "ELM_PI_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_MODULES": "1"},
                                   text=True, capture_output=True, check=True)
            self.assertEqual("leaked", open_.stdout.strip(), open_.stderr)


class NoBareInterpreterTests(unittest.TestCase):
    # Every Python, node and npm run by install-time code and the launcher goes
    # through lib/sandbox.sh or the bundled Node by path. A bare `python3` is
    # whatever PATH says, which on a conda account is conda's.
    FILES = ("bootstrap.sh", "configure.sh", "pi", "pi.orig", "install.sh", "scripts/check.sh")
    # In command position only: start of line, after $( | ; & ( exec then do,
    # optionally behind VAR=value assignments. Prose in messages is not code.
    COMMAND = re.compile(
        r"(?:^\s*|\$\(\s*|[|;&]\s*|\(\s*|\bexec\s+|\bthen\s+|\bdo\s+)"
        r"(?:\w+=\S*\s+)*(?:python3?|npm|npx|node)\s"
    )
    HEREDOC = re.compile(r"<<-?\s*'?(\w+)'?")

    def test_no_bare_interpreter_invocations(self):
        offenders = []
        for rel in self.FILES:
            terminator = None
            for number, line in enumerate((ROOT / rel).read_text().splitlines(), 1):
                if terminator:   # heredoc bodies are Python or help text
                    if line.strip() == terminator:
                        terminator = None
                    continue
                if line.lstrip().startswith("#"):
                    continue
                if self.COMMAND.search(line.split(" #")[0]):
                    offenders.append(f"{rel}:{number}: {line.strip()}")
                heredoc = self.HEREDOC.search(line)
                if heredoc:
                    terminator = heredoc.group(1)
        self.assertEqual([], offenders)

class ProxyResolutionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """The proxy is found per request, from the environment then live port files."""

    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.shim = load_shim("elm_pi_shim_proxy")
        cls.listener = socket.socket()
        cls.listener.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        cls.listener.listen(16)
        cls.live = cls.listener.getsockname()[1]
        cls.other = socket.socket()
        cls.other.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        cls.other.listen(16)
        cls.live2 = cls.other.getsockname()[1]
        cls.dead = closed_port()

    @classmethod
    def tearDownClass(cls):
        cls.listener.close()
        cls.other.close()

    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.dir, True)
        env = mock.patch.dict(os.environ)
        env.start()
        self.addCleanup(env.stop)
        for key in PROXY_VARS:
            os.environ.pop(key, None)
        glob = mock.patch.object(self.shim, "PROXY_GLOB", str(self.dir / "elm-pi-egress-*.port"))
        glob.start()
        self.addCleanup(glob.stop)
        self.shim._proxy_cached = None

    def port_file(self, name, content, age=0):
        path = self.dir / f"elm-pi-egress-{name}.port"
        path.write_text(content)
        stamp = time.time() - age
        os.utime(path, (stamp, stamp))

    def test_accepting_live_url(self):
        self.assertTrue(self.shim._accepting(f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.live}"))

    def test_accepting_with_credentials_and_slash(self):
        self.assertTrue(self.shim._accepting(f"http://user:pw@127.0.0.1:{self.live}/"))

    def test_accepting_without_scheme(self):
        self.assertTrue(self.shim._accepting(f"127.0.0.1:{self.live}"))

    def test_accepting_empty_host_means_loopback(self):
        self.assertTrue(self.shim._accepting(f"http://:{self.live}"))

    def test_not_accepting_closed_port(self):
        self.assertFalse(self.shim._accepting(f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.dead}"))

    def test_not_accepting_url_without_port(self):
        self.assertFalse(self.shim._accepting("http://127.0.0.1"))

    def test_candidates_env_order_then_newest_file(self):
        os.environ.update({"http_proxy": "http://h4:4", "HTTPS_PROXY": "http://h1:1",
                           "HTTP_PROXY": "http://h3:3", "https_proxy": "http://h2:2"})
        self.port_file("old", "1111\n", age=100)
        self.port_file("new", "2222\n", age=1)
        self.assertEqual(["http://h1:1", "http://h2:2", "http://h3:3", "http://h4:4",
                          "http://127.0.0.1:2222", "http://127.0.0.1:1111"],
                         list(self.shim._proxy_candidates()))

    def test_candidates_skip_unreadable_port_files(self):
        self.port_file("junk", "not a port", age=1)
        self.port_file("empty", "", age=2)
        self.port_file("good", "  3333 \n", age=3)
        self.assertEqual(["http://127.0.0.1:3333"], list(self.shim._proxy_candidates()))

    def test_resolve_skips_dead_env_proxy_for_live_port_file(self):
        os.environ["HTTPS_PROXY"] = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.dead}"
        self.port_file("s", str(self.live))
        self.assertEqual(f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.live}", self.shim.resolve_proxy())

    def test_resolve_none_when_nothing_answers(self):
        os.environ["HTTPS_PROXY"] = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.dead}"
        self.assertIsNone(self.shim.resolve_proxy())

    def test_resolve_keeps_a_live_cached_proxy(self):
        self.port_file("a", str(self.live))
        first = self.shim.resolve_proxy()
        self.port_file("b", str(self.live2), age=-10)    # newer, but the cached one still answers
        self.assertEqual(first, self.shim.resolve_proxy())

    def test_resolve_force_rereads(self):
        self.port_file("a", str(self.live), age=10)
        self.shim.resolve_proxy()
        self.port_file("b", str(self.live2))
        self.assertEqual(f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.live2}", self.shim.resolve_proxy(force=True))

    def test_resolve_drops_a_dead_cached_proxy(self):
        self.shim._proxy_cached = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.dead}"
        self.port_file("a", str(self.live))
        self.assertEqual(f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.live}", self.shim.resolve_proxy())

    def opener_proxies(self, opener):
        return [h.proxies for h in opener.handlers if type(h).__name__ == "ProxyHandler"]

    def test_unmanaged_opener_goes_direct(self):
        # No proxy handler at all - not even urllib's default one that reads HTTPS_PROXY.
        os.environ["HTTPS_PROXY"] = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.live}"
        with mock.patch.object(self.shim, "PROXY_MANAGED", False):
            self.assertEqual([], self.opener_proxies(self.shim._build_opener()))

    def test_managed_opener_uses_live_proxy(self):
        self.port_file("a", str(self.live))
        url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.live}"
        with mock.patch.object(self.shim, "PROXY_MANAGED", True):
            self.assertEqual([{"http": url, "https": url}], self.opener_proxies(self.shim._build_opener()))

    def test_managed_without_proxy_refuses_to_go_direct(self):
        with mock.patch.object(self.shim, "PROXY_MANAGED", True):
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "no live elm-pi egress proxy"):
                self.shim._build_opener()

class PassthroughTests(ShimServerCase):
    """Everything that does not need the shim goes to ELM exactly as sent."""

    def check(self, path, body):
        raw = json.dumps(body, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
        self.reply_with(b'{"passed":true}', ctype="application/json; charset=utf-8")
        status, headers, reply = self.request("POST", path, raw)
        self.assertEqual((200, b'{"passed":true}'), (status, reply))
        self.assertEqual("application/json; charset=utf-8", headers["content-type"])
        self.assertEqual(raw, self.upstream.requests[0]["body"])
        self.assertEqual("/api/v1" + path[len("/v1"):], self.upstream.requests[0]["path"])

    def test_invalid_json_body_forwarded_raw(self):
        self.reply_with(b"{}")
        self.request("POST", "/v1/chat/completions", b"not json {")
        self.assertEqual(b"not json {", self.upstream.requests[0]["body"])

    def test_get_forwarded_with_query(self):
        self.reply_with({"data": [{"id": LLAMA}]})
        status, _, body = self.request("GET", "/v1/models?x=1")
        self.assertEqual((200, {"data": [{"id": LLAMA}]}), (status, json.loads(body)))
        self.assertEqual(("GET", "/api/v1/models?x=1"),
                         (self.upstream.requests[0]["method"], self.upstream.requests[0]["path"]))

    def test_get_error_status_forwarded(self):
        self.reply_with({"error": "no"}, status=404)
        status, _, body = self.request("GET", "/v1/nothing")
        self.assertEqual((404, {"error": "no"}), (status, json.loads(body)))

    def test_post_error_status_forwarded(self):
        self.reply_with({"error": {"message": "bad key"}}, status=401)
        status, _, body = self.request("POST", "/v1/chat/completions", {"model": QWEN, "messages": []})
        self.assertEqual((401, "bad key"), (status, json.loads(body)["error"]["message"]))

    def test_streaming_passthrough_is_byte_identical_and_chunked(self):
        stream = b"".join(b'data: {"i":%d,"pad":"%s"}\n\n' % (i, b"x" * 300) for i in range(20)) + b"data: [DONE]\n\n"
        self.reply_with(stream, ctype="text/event-stream")
        status, headers, body = self.request("POST", "/v1/chat/completions",
                                             {"model": QWEN, "stream": True, "messages": []})
        self.assertEqual((200, "chunked", "text/event-stream", stream),
                         (status, headers.get("transfer-encoding"), headers["content-type"], body))

    def test_health_is_answered_only_for_get(self):
        self.reply_with(b'{"upstream":true}')
        status, _, body = self.request("POST", self.shim.HEALTH_PATH, b"{}")
        self.assertEqual(b'{"upstream":true}', body)
        self.assertEqual("/api/v1" + self.shim.HEALTH_PATH, self.upstream.requests[0]["path"])


add_cases(PassthroughTests, "passthrough", PASSTHROUGH, PassthroughTests.check)


class HealthTests(ShimServerCase):
    """The health endpoint identifies this shim and is never forwarded."""

    def health(self, path=None):
        status, _, body = self.request("GET", path or self.shim.HEALTH_PATH)
        self.assertEqual(200, status)
        return json.loads(body)

    def test_identifies_as_elm_pi(self):
        self.assertEqual("elm-pi", self.health()["shim"])

    def test_reports_pid_port_and_upstream(self):
        body = self.health()
        self.assertEqual((os.getpid(), self.port, f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.upstream.port}/api/v1"),
                         (body["pid"], body["port"], body["upstream"]))

    def test_reports_shimmed_models(self):
        self.assertEqual([LLAMA, EUROLLM], self.health()["models"])

    def test_unmanaged_reports_no_proxy(self):
        body = self.health()
        self.assertEqual((False, None, ""), (body["proxyManaged"], body["proxy"], body["proxyFromEnv"]))

    def test_query_string_still_health(self):
        self.assertEqual("elm-pi", self.health(self.shim.HEALTH_PATH + "?probe=1")["shim"])
        self.assertEqual([], self.upstream.requests)

class PlainLineAuthorityTests(RequestLineCase):
    """Authorities urllib reads as an allowed host that the proxy must not
    read as anything wider: userinfo, and hosts hidden in query or fragment."""


def _hidden_host_case(allowed_host, uri_fmt, dial_host):
    def test(self):
        uri = uri_fmt.format(h=allowed_host)
        proxy, client, tunnels, dials, _ = self.run_line(SHIPPED, ("GET %s HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n" % uri).encode())
        parts = urllib.parse.urlsplit(uri)
        self.assertEqual(dial_host, parts.hostname)
        # The proxy's host is the authority as written; when that is not
        # urllib's host, the proxy refuses rather than guessing.
        if reference_allowed(SHIPPED, parts.hostname) and "@" not in parts.netloc:
            self.assertEqual([(parts.hostname, parts.port or 80)], dials)
        else:
            self.assertEqual([], dials)
            self.assertEqual(1, len(self.log_lines(proxy)))
            self.assertTrue(self.log_lines(proxy)[0].startswith("REJECTED "))
    return test


for _k, _h in enumerate(sorted(set(SHIPPED))[:6]):

    add_test(PlainLineAuthorityTests, "fragment_host_is_not_the_host_%s" % slug(_h),

class PlainLineBugTests(RequestLineCase):
    """Absolute URIs the proxy reads differently from urllib."""

    # Was a bug: an empty port ("http://pypi.org:/", which RFC 3986 allows and
    # urllib reads as the default port) was taken as part of the host, so the
    # listed host was refused as "pypi.org::80".
    def test_empty_port_is_the_default_port(self):
        _, _, _, dials, _ = self.run_line(SHIPPED, b"GET http://pypi.org:/simple/ HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n")
        self.assertEqual([("pypi.org", 80)], dials)

    def test_empty_port_does_not_widen_the_allowlist(self):
        for uri, host in ((b"http://evil.org:/", "evil.org"), (b"http://[2001:db8::1]:/", "2001:db8::1"),
                          (b"http://pypi.org.evil.org:/", "pypi.org.evil.org")):
            proxy, client, tunnels, dials, _ = self.run_line(SHIPPED, b"GET " + uri + b" HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n")
            self.assert_refused(proxy, client, tunnels, dials, host, "80")


class OpenModeLineTests(RequestLineCase):
    """In open mode every generated line is let through and each host is
    recorded once, however many times and spellings it arrives in."""


def _open_lines_case(hosts, seed):
    def test(self):
        rng = random.Random(seed)
        proxy = egress.Proxy(["*"], os.path.join(self.tmp, "open.log"))
        tunnels = []
        proxy.connect_through = lambda client, host, port, head, pending=b"": tunnels.append((host, port))
        order, sent = [], 0
        for _ in range(3):
            for host in hosts:
                spelt = rng.choice([host, host.upper(), host + "."])
                client = FakeClient(("CONNECT %s:%s HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n" % (bracket(spelt), rng.choice(PORTS))).encode())
                proxy.handle(client, ("127.0.0.1", 0))
                sent += 1
                key = spelt.lower().rstrip(".")
                if key not in order:
                    order.append(key)
        self.assertEqual(sent, len(tunnels))
        self.assertEqual(["OPEN     %s no allowlist in this install (--allow '*')" % h for h in order],
                         self.log_lines(proxy))
    return test
